sched.jobs.attribute-sources.refresh.des: Reads the next page of the realm's people from each attribute source whose scheduled interval is due, onto their entries (#94). attributeSources.refreshBatch people per source per run.
sched.jobs.authn.account-set-expiry.desc: Brings every browser's account set up to date (#561): an account whose session ended is remembered as signed out, one remembered longer than authn.rememberedAccountDays is dropped, and an empty set is deleted.
sched.jobs.authn.session-expiry.title: Session expiry
sched.jobs.authn.session-expiry.describe: Ends every sign-on session whose lifetime or idle timeout has passed, and, in each realm, at most that realm's authn.sessionShedPerSweep of one subject's own surplus sessions.
sched.jobs.caches.eject-expired.title: Expired cache entries ejection
sched.jobs.caches.eject-expired.describe: Deletes, in this process, every cache and replay-store entry whose lifetime has passed — housekeeping only: each store still refuses an expired entry where it reads it.
sched.jobs.cluster.claims-purge.title: Expired claims sweep
sched.jobs.cluster.claims-purge.describe: Deletes the single-use claims whose lifetime has passed from the table every node shares.
sched.jobs.cluster.node-snapshot.title: Node snapshot
sched.jobs.cluster.node-snapshot.describ: Writes this node's Monitoring → Worker Pools and → Node Health views to the shared store, one row per node name, so every node draws every node on those pages (#332).
sched.jobs.cluster.node-snapshot-purge.d: Deletes the Worker Pools and Node Health snapshot of a node that is no longer a live cluster member once it is older than cluster.nodeSnapshotRetentionHours; never a live member's, and nothing while membership cannot be read (#332).
sched.jobs.cluster.rate-window-purge.des: Deletes the rate-limit windows that have passed from the table every node shares.
sched.jobs.devices.android-status-rechec: Asks the active Android attestation status list about every stored Android chain — device keys and WebAuthn credentials, in every realm — and downgrades the ones it revokes or suspends: self-asserted, audited, CAEP credential-change. Reads only the people and devices marked as holding one, a page at a time, and skips a realm where neither the list nor the registrations moved since its last recheck. Run when a list is activated, and daily.
sched.jobs.devices.android-status-refres: Downloads Google's Android key attestation status list from devices.androidStatusUrl and loads it as the risk dataset android.attestation-status: which attestation certificates are revoked or suspended. Daily (devices.androidStatusRefreshS); a list identical to the active one loads nothing.
sched.jobs.federation.encryption-key-ret: Removes from each federation relationship the encryption key a rotation replaced, once federation.encryptionKeyGraceS has passed. The key stopped decrypting at that instant already; this takes it off the entry.
sched.jobs.federation.provision-idle.des: Disables a person whose only sign-in path is one federation relationship, once federationLastSeen is older than that relationship's fedProvisionIdleMinutes. Empty or 0 leaves everybody. The entry and the link are kept. A local password, or a link through another relationship, is left alone.
sched.jobs.gnap.grant-expiry.title: GNAP: expired grants
sched.jobs.gnap.grant-expiry.describe: Finalizes each GNAP grant whose interaction or grant lifetime (gnap.grantLifetimeS) has ended and that no request has touched since, recording why (#432).
sched.jobs.gnap.spend-purge.title: GNAP: limits of ended grants
sched.jobs.gnap.spend-purge.describe: Deletes the running totals kept for each GNAP grant's limits once the grant has ended, when no token of it can be presented (#432).
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-count.title: Data encryption key value counts
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-count.describe: Counts the values sealed under every data encryption key, in one pass of the store, and keeps each count on its key for /admin/encryption.
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-reencrypt.title: Data re-encryption and key destruction
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-reencrypt.descr: Re-seals every value still sealed under a superseded data encryption key under the current one, and destroys a superseded key once nothing is sealed under it and it has been superseded for keys.dataKeyRetireAfterDays.
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-rotate.title: Data encryption key rotation
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-rotate.describe: Gives every data encryption key that has sealed new values for keys.dataKeyRotationDays a successor, published keys.dataKeyActivationLeadSeconds before anything is sealed under it; the re-encryption job then re-seals what the old key sealed.
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-rotate-now.titl: Data encryption key rotation, by hand
sched.jobs.keys.data-key-rotate-now.desc: Rotates every stored data encryption key now — or one realm's, or one class's; the keys they replace go on opening what they sealed until it is re-sealed.
sched.jobs.keys.kek-rotate-now.title: Key-encryption key rotation, by hand
sched.jobs.keys.kek-rotate-now.describe: Makes a new version of the key-encryption key in its key management service and re-wraps every data encryption key under it. Only for a key in a KMS.
sched.jobs.krb5.krbtgt-rotate.title: krbtgt key rotation
sched.jobs.krb5.krbtgt-rotate.describe: Replaces each realm's krbtgt key — the key every TGT is sealed under — with a new random one at the next kvno once it is krb5.krbtgtRotationIntervalDays old, keeping the one it replaces for the longest a TGT under it can live, and never while the version the last rotation kept is still in its window. Gives a product realm with none its first key. Each run's result names the kvno, the last rotation and when the next is due.
sched.jobs.krb5.krbtgt-rotate-now.title: krbtgt key rotation, by hand
sched.jobs.krb5.krbtgt-rotate-now.descri: Rotates the realm's krbtgt key now. With invalidate, keeps no previous version: every TGT issued before it is refused and a Shared Signals event says so.
sched.jobs.mail.deliver.title: Mail outbox delivery
sched.jobs.mail.deliver.describe: Sends every queued message that is due — a retry whose backoff has passed, a lease that lapsed, a row restored after a restart — dead-letters any still pending past mail.retentionS, and removes finished rows past it.
sched.jobs.oauth2.backchannel-logout-swe: Sends every Logout Token delivery that is due — a retry whose backoff has passed, a lease that lapsed, a row restored after a restart — and dead-letters any still pending past oauth2.backchannelLogoutRetentionS.
sched.jobs.oauth2.ciba-sweep.title: CIBA sweep
sched.jobs.oauth2.ciba-sweep.describe: Attempts every CIBA ping and push that is due, dead-letters one still pending past oauth2.cibaNotifyRetentionS, expires backchannel authentication requests nobody answered in time, and drops what finished more than an hour ago.
Refreshes each person's token at a Claims Provider they linked before it expires, and drops link requests nobody finished (#147).
sched.jobs.oauth2.client-secret-expiry.d: Checks every client secret of every application: an audit row for an application holding one that expires within oauth2.clientSecretExpiryWarningDays, and for one whose every secret has expired; and removes the expired secrets an application holds an unexpired one beside — never its last, which stays and is refused in product.
sched.jobs.oauth2.command-sweep.title: OpenID Provider Commands sweep
sched.jobs.oauth2.command-sweep.describe: Sends every Command Token delivery that is due — a retry whose backoff has passed, a lease that lapsed, a row restored after a restart — dead-letters any still pending past oauth2.commandRetentionS, and drops expired callback tokens and finished tenant runs.
sched.jobs.oauth2.device-code-sweep.desc: Expires RFC 8628 device codes nobody approved in time, and removes those that finished more than an hour ago (#150).
sched.jobs.oauth2.ephemeral-subjects-pur: Removes each ephemeral subject identifier whose tokens and session can no longer be in use (#149).
sched.jobs.oauth2.expired-token-purge.de: Deletes the token records past their expiry and oauth2.expiredTokenRetentionS, and the revocations of tokens that have expired.
sched.jobs.oauth2.grant-management-purge: Removes each OAuth grant whose last token has expired, and the record of each token minted under a grant once it expires (#142).
sched.jobs.oauth2.token-holders-backfill: Notes the holder of every token already issued on the users list, once per realm, now that the token register is read on demand (#820).
sched.jobs.oauth2.used-assertion-purge.d: Deletes the RFC 7523 and RFC 7522 assertions whose lifetime has passed from the once-ever history every node shares.
sched.jobs.oidfed.collection-crawl.title: OpenID Federation Entity Collection crawl
sched.jobs.oidfed.collection-crawl.descr: Walks every entity beneath the realm — each resolved to the realm before its own list is fetched — and keeps what it finds for the collection endpoint (#136).
sched.jobs.oidfed.key-rotate.title: OpenID Federation key rotation
sched.jobs.oidfed.key-rotate.describe: Keeps each realm's Federation Entity Keys one rotation ahead — a next key published before it signs — and rotates once the current key is older than oidfed.keyRotationDays and the next has been published for the whole oidfed.keyOverlapDays.
sched.jobs.oidfed.key-rotate-now.title: OpenID Federation key rotation, by hand
sched.jobs.oidfed.key-rotate-now.describ: Rotates the realm's Federation Entity Key now — or, as an emergency, revokes the current and next keys as compromised and replaces them.
sched.jobs.oidfed.registrations-expire.d: Removes each client registered through an OpenID Federation Trust Chain whose registration has ended (12.3). Every endpoint already answers such a client as unknown; this only stops the entry lingering.
sched.jobs.persistence.minted-expiry-pur: Deletes from the shared store, in batches of 5000 and at most 20 batches of each kind per run, the minted rows no start will read again: past their own expiry, of a realm that is no longer defined (written over an hour ago), and a short-lived store's rows with no expiry older than persistence.mintedRetention.
sched.jobs.persistence.tombstone-purge.d: Deletes the tombstones of ended minted rows older than persistence.mintedRetention from the shared store.
sched.jobs.process.memory-report.title: Memory report
sched.jobs.process.memory-report.describ: Logs, in this process, one line with its role and its memory: resident size, heap used and total, the heap limit, external memory and array buffers (#341).
sched.jobs.risc.opt-out-effective.title: RISC opt-outs becoming effective
sched.jobs.risc.opt-out-effective.descri: Sends RISC opt-out-effective for every account whose holder opted out on /portal/signals at least risc.optOutDelayHours ago and did not cancel (RISC 1.0 section 2.8), which moves the account to the opt-out state.
sched.jobs.risk.dataset-directory.title: Risk dataset directory import
sched.jobs.risk.dataset-directory.descri: Imports each dataset an operator put in risk.datasetsDirectory, by its manifest, verifying and activating it; a version already recorded is not loaded again.
sched.jobs.risk.mds-refresh.title: FIDO metadata download
sched.jobs.risk.mds-refresh.describe: Downloads the FIDO MDS3 BLOB from risk.mdsUrl and imports it when its serial is newer than the active one — verified to the FIDO root, its chain's revocation checked, under a recorded acceptance of the fido-mds3 terms. Daily (risk.mdsRefreshS), hourly once the active BLOB is past its own nextUpdate.
sched.jobs.risk.rescore.title: Risk re-check of live sessions
sched.jobs.risk.rescore.describe: Re-checks every live sign-on session against the active datasets and the failure history, and raises the risk of one that has become riskier — an address now on a Tor or deny list, a password being guessed — so every token on it is decided on the new risk, and a person crossing into HIGH is answered by the risk-response policy.
sched.jobs.risk.retention.title: Risk retention
sched.jobs.risk.retention.describe: Deletes the rows of dataset versions superseded more than risk.supersededRetentionDays ago and of refused versions, the failures older than risk.failureRetentionDays, and the assessments and the model's history past risk.assessmentRetentionDays and risk.historyRetentionDays.
sched.jobs.risk.stalled-imports.title: Stalled risk imports
sched.jobs.risk.stalled-imports.describe: Marks refused (STS-RISK-0035) every dataset version left loading with no progress for risk.importStallMinutes — an import whose process stopped part-way — and drops whatever rows it had written.
sched.jobs.risk.upload-cleanup.title: Risk upload clean-up
sched.jobs.risk.upload-cleanup.describe: In every process: keeps the dataset uploads this process is importing fresh, and deletes from risk.uploadDirectory an upload no live process has touched for risk.importStallMinutes — what a process that stopped mid-import left behind.
sched.jobs.scheduler.history.title: Scheduler run history
sched.jobs.scheduler.history.describe: Keeps, per job, its last scheduler.runHistoryCount runs or its last scheduler.runHistoryHours, whichever is more, and always its latest run; deletes the rest — and every row naming a realm that was removed — in batches of 2000, at most 25 a run.
sched.jobs.scim-client.deliver.title: Outbound SCIM deliveries
sched.jobs.scim-client.deliver.describe: Sends every outbound SCIM client's due deliveries — new changes and retries alike — to its service provider, scimClient.concurrency at a time, skipping a client while it is paused by its backoff, and keeps the queues to their retention (#552).
sched.jobs.scim-client.reconcile.title: Outbound SCIM reconciliations
sched.jobs.scim-client.reconcile.describ: Reconciles each outbound SCIM client whose scimClientReconcileMinutes has come round: every person and group in its scope is pushed, and what its service provider holds under an externalId of this realm's and no longer in scope is deprovisioned (#552).
sched.jobs.service-accounts.previous-cle: Clears a rotated service account's previous password once its overlap has ended. The overlap is checked where the password is read, so this is housekeeping.
sched.jobs.service-accounts.rotate.title: Service-account password rotation
sched.jobs.service-accounts.rotate.descr: Gives every service account that names a push destination a new password once its interval has passed (the service-account policy): pushed to the destination first, committed only after the push succeeded, the previous password accepted for the overlap. A failed push changes nothing.
sched.jobs.service-accounts.rotate-now.d: Rotates one service account's password now, as the hourly job would: push first, then commit.
sched.jobs.signing.retire.title: Retired signing key clean-up
sched.jobs.signing.retire.describe: Drops every retired signing key whose grace has passed and supersedes its certificate on its Issuing CA's list.
sched.jobs.signing.rotate.title: Signing key rotation
sched.jobs.signing.rotate.describe: Gives every signing unit of the realm a next key, published before it signs anything, and promotes each next key once it has been published for a whole interval (signing.rotationIntervalDays); the key it replaces goes on verifying through its grace.
sched.jobs.signing.rotate-now.title: Signing key rotation, by hand
sched.jobs.signing.rotate-now.describe: Rotates the named signing units of the realm — or every one — now: each next key becomes current and the key it replaces is retired, verifying through its grace.
sched.jobs.spiffe.authority-rotation.des: Rotates the realm's SPIFFE X.509 authority once it is past half its lifetime and its JWT authority once it is older than half spiffe.caTtl; the old ones stay published (spiffe.retainedAuthorities).
sched.jobs.spiffe.sigstore-tuf-refresh.d: Fetches the sigstore trust root (Fulcio CAs, Rekor and CT log keys) through TUF for the docker workload attestor's image-signature checks; a refresh that fails keeps the last verified set.
sched.jobs.spiffe.target-reconcile.title: SPIFFE target reconcile
sched.jobs.spiffe.target-reconcile.descr: Registers each running task's private address in this cluster's SPIFFE target groups and deregisters an address no running task still has (#323).
sched.jobs.ssf.dead-letter-sweep.title: Shared Signals dead-letter sweep
sched.jobs.ssf.dead-letter-sweep.describ: Deletes this process's expired dead letters, probes dead streams that are due (one node only) and logs the summary of what was dead-lettered since the last sweep.
sched.jobs.ssf.foreign-poll.title: Federation partners' Shared Signals poll
sched.jobs.ssf.foreign-poll.describe: Polls every federation relationship whose partner's Shared Signals stream is a poll stream (RFC 8936): the Security Event Tokens it holds are verified, acted on and acknowledged.
sched.jobs.ssf.internal-poll.title: Console and portal Shared Signals poll
sched.jobs.ssf.internal-poll.describe: This service's own admin console and user portal collect the Security Event Tokens waiting on their streams, in every realm, over RFC 8936 poll from /ssf/poll — verified, recorded, acted on and acknowledged (#771).
sched.jobs.ssf.stream-maintenance.title: Shared Signals stream maintenance
sched.jobs.ssf.stream-maintenance.descri: Pauses, disables or deletes a stream whose receiver has been inactive for ssf.inactivityTimeoutS (SSF 1.0 section 8.1.1), announcing a pause or disable with a stream-updated event first, and sends a verification event to every enabled stream that has had none from this transmitter for ssf.verificationEveryS (section 8.1.4).
sched.jobs.tls.ticket-key-rotate.title: TLS session-ticket key rotation
sched.jobs.tls.ticket-key-rotate.describ: Replaces the session-ticket key every node's TLS listeners share in an active-active cluster, so a ticket one node issued resumes on another. The key it replaces is deleted, which bounds how long a resumed session's secrets can be recovered from a ticket.
sched.sentence.overdueTicking: the leader is ticking; a previous run may still be going, or its claim has not lapsed
sched.sentence.offZero: {{setting}} is 0, so the job is off
sched.sentence.offZeroFixed: its interval is 0, so the job is off
schedAdmin.message.steppedDown: The scheduler's leader was asked to stand down. It does so at its next tick, and another node takes the lead at its next heartbeat.
schedAdmin.message.queued: A run of {{job}} is queued. The scheduler's leader starts it at its next tick.
schedAdmin.message.queuedAgain: A run of {{job}} is queued (one already was; this is it). The scheduler's leader starts it at its next tick.
